author_note: Labelled purely from procurement business sense without seeing the system. Each case is built from valid identifiers from idgen.py (typos made by altering one digit / transposing). Approved cases deliberately include harmless variations (Pvt Ltd vs PRIVATE LIMITED, umlauts, M/s prefix, DBA titles, UG (haftungsbeschraenkt), IBAN-only GB, sole proprietor in own name, swapped upload slots, shared office building, near-miss sanctions name, 88-day letter, years-old GST certificate) to catch over-alerting. Reviewer cases target real fraud patterns: re-registration of existing vendors with new bank details, lookalike domains, shared bank accounts/EINs, altered PDFs, third-party or personal payee accounts, borrowed tax IDs, letterhead/IBAN inconsistency, and mixed fixable+fraud cases (fraud wins). Vendor-fixable cases are honest gaps: missing/wrong/old/blurry documents, blanks, checksum typos, wrong dropdowns. Rejections cover exact, alias, punctuation-variant and payee-side sanctions hits.

cases.title: IN clean private limited
cases.story: Mumbai packaging supplier submits a complete form with a GST certificate PDF and a recent bank confirmation letter; everything matches.

form.address: Unit 7, Andheri Industrial Estate, Andheri East

printed.address: Unit 7, Andheri Industrial Estate, Andheri East, Mumbai 400001

cases.why: All fields complete and consistent with both documents; nothing unusual.

cases.title: DE clean GmbH, German documents
cases.story: Berlin electrical contractor; VAT confirmation from the Bundeszentralamt fuer Steuern and a Bankbestaetigung, both in German.
cases.why: German-language documents are expected for a German vendor and every value matches the form.

cases.title: GB clean Ltd
cases.story: Manchester metal fabricator with sort code and account number, HMRC VAT certificate and a Lloyds confirmation letter.

printed.address: Unit 3, Ancoats Works, Redhill Street, Manchester M1 1AE

cases.why: Complete and consistent submission.

cases.title: US clean LLC
cases.story: Austin fleet maintenance LLC submits W-9 and a bank account verification letter that match the form.

printed.address: 2200 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78701

cases.why: Complete, consistent W-9 and bank letter.

cases.title: Pvt Ltd vs PRIVATE LIMITED, old GST cert
cases.story: Form says 'Pvt Ltd'; the GST certificate (issued almost 4 years ago) and the photographed cancelled cheque print the name in capitals as 'PRIVATE LIMITED'.
cases.why: Abbreviation/case differences are harmless and a GST registration certificate does not expire; only the bank proof needs to be recent, and it is.

cases.title: IN sole proprietor paid in own name
cases.story: Proprietorship 'Kumar Electricals'; GST certificate shows legal name Ramesh Kumar with that trade name, and the bank account is in Ramesh Kumar's own name. Uses a Gmail address.
cases.why: For a sole proprietorship the proprietor is the legal entity, so a personal-name account and a free email address are normal; all identifiers agree.

cases.title: DE umlaut transliteration
cases.story: Form typed with ASCII 'Mueller' and 'Strasse'; the German documents print 'Müller' and 'Straße'.
cases.why: ue/ü and ss/ß are the same name in German; everything else matches.

cases.title: GB pays via IBAN only
cases.story: Edinburgh textile firm leaves sort code/account number blank and supplies an IBAN plus SWIFT instead; RBS letter shows IBAN and sort code.
cases.why: Policy explicitly allows an IBAN in place of sort code + account number, and the IBAN matches the letter.

cases.title: US account titled with DBA
cases.story: Seattle company declares trade name 'CascadeSig'; the bank account title is 'Cascade Signal Systems Inc DBA CascadeSig'.

form.account_holder: Cascade Signal Systems Inc DBA CascadeSig

printed.account_holder: Cascade Signal Systems Inc DBA CascadeSig

cases.why: The account is held by the same legal entity with its declared DBA; that is a normal title.

cases.title: IN partnership firm with M/s prefix
cases.story: Jaipur partnership firm; the cancelled cheque reads 'M/S SHARMA AND SONS' and the GST certificate 'Sharma and Sons'.
cases.why: 'M/s' is a customary Indian honorific for firms and '&' vs 'and' is cosmetic; identifiers match.

cases.title: DE bank letter 88 days old
cases.story: Hamburg refrigeration AG; the Sparkasse confirmation letter is 88 days old, close to but inside the 90-day window.
cases.why: 88 days is within the 90-day validity window.

cases.title: GB shares building with existing vendor
cases.story: New Bristol vendor is a tenant in the same office building as existing vendor Brightpath Consulting (12 Quay Street), but has its own VAT, bank and contact.
cases.why: A shared multi-tenant address alone is not suspicious when name, tax ID, bank and contact are all distinct.

cases.title: US punctuation and case differences
cases.story: Form says 'Redwood Analytics, Inc.'; W-9 says 'REDWOOD ANALYTICS INC' and the bank letter 'Redwood Analytics Incorporated'.
cases.why: Punctuation, capitalisation and Inc/Incorporated are the same entity.

cases.title: DE UG without (haftungsbeschraenkt) on form
cases.story: Form says 'Kleinwerk UG'; documents print the full legal form 'Kleinwerk UG (haftungsbeschränkt)'.
cases.why: The parenthetical is part of the legal-form suffix, not a different company.

cases.title: GB clean plc with SWIFT
cases.story: Birmingham plc with sort code, account number and SWIFT; HSBC letter and VAT certificate all match.
cases.why: Complete and consistent; a clear photo of the letter is acceptable.

cases.title: US voided check
cases.story: Atlanta coatings corporation uploads a W-9 PDF and a photographed voided check.
cases.why: A voided check is acceptable bank proof and matches the form.

cases.title: US name resembles a sanctioned entity
cases.story: A Denver bakery whose name shares 'Orion Va...' with sanctioned 'Orion Vale Metals LLC', but nothing else in common.
cases.why: A superficial name similarity to a sanctioned metals trader is not a match; different name, industry and identifiers.

cases.title: IN swapped upload slots, common contact name
cases.story: Kochi exporter put the bank letter in the tax slot and the GST certificate in the bank slot; contact person is 'Priya Nair', the same common name as an existing vendor's contact.
cases.why: Both required documents were provided and match, just in each other's slots; a common personal name is not a duplicate signal.

cases.title: IN missing bank proof
cases.story: Complete form and GST certificate, but no bank proof was uploaded.
cases.why: Required bank proof is missing; vendor just needs to upload it.

cases.title: DE bank letter too old
cases.story: Munich print shop; Bankbestaetigung is 140 days old.
cases.why: Bank proof older than 90 days; vendor must provide a recent one.

cases.title: GB invoice uploaded instead of VAT certificate
cases.story: London caterer uploaded one of its sales invoices (which shows its VAT number) into the tax certificate slot.
cases.why: An invoice is not a VAT registration certificate; the vendor must upload the right document.

cases.title: US blurry W-9 photo
cases.story: Columbus pallet supplier photographed its W-9 at an angle; the image is too blurry to read.
cases.why: Tax form is unreadable; vendor should re-upload a clear copy.

cases.title: IN account number digits transposed
cases.story: Two adjacent digits of the account number are swapped on the form; the cancelled cheque (same bank, IFSC and holder) shows the correct number.
cases.why: Classic keying error with everything else matching; vendor should correct the form rather than anyone paying the typed number.

cases.title: DE IBAN typo fails checksum
cases.story: One digit of the IBAN is mistyped on the form (fails the IBAN check); the bank letter shows the correct IBAN for the same holder.
cases.why: Invalid IBAN from a typo is a vendor-fixable data error; nothing suspicious.

cases.title: GB VAT number left blank
cases.story: Leeds joinery left the VAT number field empty though its VAT certificate is attached.
cases.why: Required form field missing; vendor fills it in.

cases.title: US SSN-shaped number in EIN field
cases.story: The LLC typed what looks like a personal SSN (NNN-NN-NNNN) in the EIN field; the W-9 shows a proper company EIN.
cases.why: Tax ID field is in the wrong format and doesn't match the W-9; vendor should enter the EIN.

cases.title: IN bank statement as bank proof
cases.story: Chennai chemicals firm uploaded a recent bank statement instead of a bank letter or cancelled cheque.
cases.why: Policy accepts only a bank confirmation letter or cancelled cheque; vendor should upload one of those.

cases.title: DE utility bill as bank proof
cases.story: Cologne furniture maker uploaded an electricity bill (Stromrechnung) in the bank proof slot.
cases.why: Wrong document type for bank proof; vendor re-uploads.

cases.title: GB contact email missing
cases.story: Everything provided except the contact email address.
cases.why: Required field missing.

cases.title: US vendor selects EUR currency
cases.story: Denver surveying firm with a US bank account chose EUR as currency in the form dropdown.
cases.why: A domestic US ACH account in EUR is inconsistent; most likely a dropdown slip the vendor should correct.

cases.title: IN GSTIN typo fails checksum
cases.story: One digit of the GSTIN is mistyped on the form; the GST certificate shows the valid GSTIN.
cases.why: Invalid GSTIN from a typo; certificate shows the right one, vendor corrects the field.

cases.title: DE no VAT certificate uploaded
cases.story: Form and bank letter fine, VAT registration certificate not uploaded.
cases.why: Required tax document missing.

cases.title: GB bank letter 91 days old
cases.story: Bank letter is 91 days old, one day past the window.
cases.why: Just outside the 90-day window; vendor needs a fresh letter.

cases.title: IN wrong entity type picked
cases.story: A private limited company (PAN shows company type, name ends 'Pvt Ltd') selected 'sole_prop' in the entity-type dropdown.
cases.why: Entity type contradicts the name and GSTIN; a form error the vendor can fix.

cases.title: IN existing vendor re-registers with new bank
cases.story: A submission using existing vendor Globex's exact name, GSTIN and address, but a new Yes Bank account and a Gmail contact.

printed.address: Plot 14, MIDC Industrial Area, Mumbai, Mumbai 400001

cases.why: Duplicate of an approved vendor with changed bank details is the classic payment-diversion pattern; must be verified with the known contact.

cases.title: DE lookalike email domain for existing vendor
cases.story: Same name, VAT ID and contact person as existing vendor Northwind, but a hyphenated lookalike email domain and a new Commerzbank IBAN.
cases.why: Lookalike domain plus new bank account for an existing vendor indicates impersonation.

cases.title: GB new vendor uses existing vendor's bank account
cases.story: New Bristol company whose sort code and account number are identical to those of existing vendor Brightpath Consulting.
cases.why: One bank account shared by two supposedly unrelated vendors suggests a shell or duplicate-payment scheme.

cases.title: US bank letter digitally altered
cases.story: The bank letter looks perfect and shows the form's account number, but the PDF contains a different account number underneath the visible one.
cases.why: A tampered bank document is a fraud signal regardless of everything matching on the surface.

cases.title: IN bank letter holder name overwritten
cases.story: Bank letter shows the company as account holder, but the PDF's underlying text names an individual (Deepak Malhotra).

printed.address: B-22 Okhla Industrial Area Phase 1, New Delhi 110001

cases.why: Altered account-holder field means the account likely belongs to a person, not the vendor.

cases.title: DE payments to a third-party factoring company
cases.story: Berlin solar installer asks to be paid into an account held by a factoring company; form and bank letter both name the factor.
cases.why: Third-party payee accounts need an assignment agreement and human verification before any payment set-up.

cases.title: GB company paid into director's personal account
cases.story: Limited company gives bank details for an account held personally by its contact/director.
cases.why: A Ltd's payments going to an individual's account is a fraud/compliance concern.

cases.title: US form bank differs from bank letter
cases.story: Form lists one bank/routing/account; the bank letter (same holder name) is for an entirely different bank and account.
cases.why: Wholly different account (not a typo) on form vs proof means the form account is unverified - a diversion pattern.

cases.title: IN GSTIN belongs to another company
cases.story: Valid GSTIN, but the attached GST certificate is for 'Zenith Castings Pvt Ltd' (and the PAN's name letter is Z, not P).
cases.why: Borrowing another entity's tax registration is identity misuse, not a simple upload mistake.

cases.title: IN same name as existing vendor, different GSTIN
cases.story: Uses the same company name as existing vendor Acme Technologies Private Limited but a different (valid) Maharashtra GSTIN, new bank and a Gmail address.
cases.why: Indian company names are unique, so a second 'Acme Technologies' with new tax ID and bank looks like impersonation.

cases.title: GB name shares core of sanctioned shipper
cases.story: London logistics company called 'Meridian Crest Logistics Ltd' - closely resembling sanctioned 'Meridian Crest Shipping Co'.
cases.why: Same distinctive name in a related industry could be an affiliate or front; needs a human sanctions check, not auto-approval or auto-rejection.

cases.title: US reuses existing vendor's EIN
cases.story: New office-supplies LLC submits the same EIN as existing vendor Summit Office Supplies LLC.
cases.why: Two different names on one EIN indicates identity reuse or a duplicate vendor.

cases.title: GB missing VAT cert and payee is a different company
cases.story: No VAT certificate uploaded (fixable) and the account is held by 'Kestrel Holdings Ltd', not the vendor.
cases.why: A third-party payee needs review; per policy the fraud-shaped signal outranks the fixable gap.

cases.title: IN stale and altered bank letter
cases.story: Bank letter is 120 days old (fixable) and its account number was digitally edited over a different original.
cases.why: Tampering trumps the staleness; must not just ask the vendor for a new letter.

cases.title: US W-9 for a different company
cases.story: Form is for Cobalt Ridge Logistics LLC; the W-9 carries the same EIN but names 'Harborline Freight Inc' at a Florida address.
cases.why: Tax document identifies a different taxpayer; identity is unverified and possibly borrowed.

cases.title: DE letterhead bank differs from IBAN's bank
cases.story: Form and bank letter say Deutsche Bank, but the IBAN's bank code belongs to Commerzbank.
cases.why: A bank letter whose letterhead can't have issued that IBAN looks forged.

cases.title: DE Bankbestaetigung with edited IBAN
cases.story: German bank confirmation scan looks normal, but the IBAN text was replaced; the original IBAN is still in the PDF.
cases.why: Document tampering on the bank account field is a fraud signal.

cases.title: GB exact sanctioned name
cases.story: Applicant's legal name exactly matches sanctioned entity DEMO-002.

printed.address: 1 Canada Square, Canary Wharf, London EC1A 1BB

cases.why: Sanctioned party; hard stop.

cases.title: IN trade name is a sanctioned alias
cases.story: Innocuous legal name, but the declared trade name (also on the GST certificate) is 'MC Shipping', an alias of sanctioned Meridian Crest Shipping Co.

printed.address: Ballard Estate, 4 Shoorji Vallabhdas Marg, Mumbai 400001

cases.why: Operating under a listed sanctions alias makes this a sanctioned party.

cases.title: US legal name is a sanctioned alias
cases.story: Legal name 'Orion Vale Metallurgy Inc' matches the listed alias of sanctioned Orion Vale Metals LLC.
cases.why: Alias match to a sanctioned entity; different suffix doesn't change that.

cases.title: DE clean vendor, payee is sanctioned
cases.story: Clean German machinery company, but the nominated bank account (form and letter) is held by Blackthorn Offshore Trading Ltd.
cases.why: Payments would flow to a sanctioned party; hard stop.

cases.title: US sanctioned name with punctuation/case
cases.story: Sanctioned 'Meridian Crest Shipping Co' written in capitals with a hyphen and trailing period.
cases.why: Formatting differences don't change an exact sanctioned-name match.
